'''Philip Moriarty''' (born 1968 in [[London]]) is an Irish [[physicist]] and professor of physics at the [[University of Nottingham]]. He is known for his work on nanostructures and his collaboration with [[Brady Haran]] on the [[YouTube]] video series [[Sixty Symbols]].

==Education and career==
From 1990 to 1994, Moriarty attended the School of Physical Sciences of [[Dublin City University]], where he received his doctorate in physics in 1994. Until 1997, he wasa postdoctoral researcher in the field of physics at the [[University of Nottingham]]. He became a lecturer in the Department of Physics until 2003. Since 2005, he has been Professor of Physics at the School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Nottingham.<ref name="The University of Nottingham">{{cite web |title=Philip Moriarty |url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/~ppzpjm/PhilipMoriaty_CV_May_2019.pdf |website=The University of Nottingham |access-date=17 August 2019 |ref=3 |archive-date=17 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190817170835/https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/~ppzpjm/PhilipMoriaty_CV_May_2019.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Moriarty is one of the collaborating members of the [[Sixty Symbols]] Internet video series, where [[Brady Haran]] interviews a scientist about some physics topic in each episode.<ref name="Sixty Symbols">{{cite web |title=The Scientists - Sixty Symbols |url=http://www.sixtysymbols.com/pages/scientists1.htm |website=Sixty Symbols |access-date=17 August 2019}}</ref> In 2016, Haran, Michael Merrifeld and Moriarty were awarded the [[Kelvin Medal and Prize]] by the [[Institute of Physics]]. The citation was "for innovative and effective promotion of the public understanding of physics through the Sixty Symbols video project."<ref>{{cite web |title=2016 Kelvin Medal and prize of the Institute of Physics |url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/kelvin/medallists/page_67620.html |publisher=Institute of Physics |access-date=28 August 2019 |archive-date=29 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190829010712/http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/kelvin/medallists/page_67620.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Moriarty is the author of ''When the Uncertainty Principle Goes to 11: Or How to Explain Quantum Physics with Heavy Metal''.<ref>{{cite book |last=Moriarty |first=Philip |date=31 July 2018 |title=When the Uncertainty Principle Goes to 11: Or How to Explain Quantum Physics with Heavy Metal |publisher=BenBella Books |isbn=978-1-944648-52-7 |author-link=Philip Moriarty |ref=4}}</ref> This book was shortlisted for [[Physics World]]'s Book Of The Year 2018.<ref name="The University of Nottingham" /> He also wrote ''Nanotechnology'' for [[Oxford University Press]]'s ''[[Very Short Introductions]]'' series.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Moriarty |first=Philip |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FbefEAAAQBAJ |title=Nanotechnology: A Very Short Introduction |date=2022-12-01 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-257790-0 |language=en}}</ref>
